new_scholarship.name: Masters International Excellence Scholarships
new_scholarship.description: The University of Leeds offers a set of merit scholarships worth £3,000, £6,000 or £16,000 to international students applying to eligible taught Master's courses starting in September 2027. The award is paid as a tuition fee discount on the first year of study only and cannot be used towards maintenance or accommodation costs. Applicants must already hold a conditional or unconditional offer and then submit a separate scholarship application; two rounds are scheduled for 28 February 2027 and 16 May 2027.
new_scholarship.application_period: Applications for September 2027 taught Master's courses open 1 October 2026; scholarship round one closes 28 February 2027 and round two 16 May 2027.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: International (non-UK) fee-status applicants holding a conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible full-time taught Master's course starting September 2027, who are self-funded or partially funded and hold a Bachelor's degree equivalent to a 2:1 (hons) or better.
eligibility: Classified as an international student for fee purposes
Hold a conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible full-time taught Master's course starting in September 2027
Be self-funded or partially-funded
Predicted or achieved minimum of a Bachelor's degree with a 2:1 (hons) or equivalent
Demonstrate an excellent academic track record
coverage: Partial tuition fee discount on the first year of study only
requirements: Scholarship application form submitted after receiving an admission offer
Demonstrate excellent professional and personal skills evidenced through work experience and/or extracurricular activities
application_method: Submit the University of Leeds scholarship application form; offer holders are notified by email with details of how to apply
A separate scholarship application is required for each course if you hold offers for multiple courses
new_scholarship.funding_period: one-off tuition fee discount on the first year of study
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Awards recognise and reward high academic achievement. The final scholarship awarded to an applicant is determined by the University and all decisions are final.
new_scholarship.notes: The MBA programme is excluded because it runs its own MBA Excellence Scholarship scheme, and all fully online courses are excluded.

new_scholarship.name: TU/e Scholarship for Excellence: Shaping the Future of Microchip Innovation
new_scholarship.program_type: University merit scholarship (funded through the national Beethoven Programme)
new_scholarship.description: Eindhoven University of Technology awards approximately 35 Scholarship for Excellence places to international students applying to selected Master's programmes in Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering and Mathematics & Computer Science for the 2027-2028 academic year. Each scholarship is worth €7,500 per academic year for two years, paid in monthly instalments, and the University states it is not a full scholarship. Consideration is part of the normal Master's application, which must be completed by 1 January 2027 with a short motivation.
new_scholarship.application_period: Academic year 2027-2028, starting 1 September 2027; complete the Master's programme application by 1 January 2027.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: International applicants who have applied for an eligible full-time TU/e Master's programme for 2027-2028, meet that programme's admission requirements, completed a non-Dutch high school diploma or bachelor's degree, have no prior Dutch higher education, hold a GPA of at least 7.5/10, and can obtain a Dutch entry visa and residence permit.
eligibility: Applied for a full-time Master's programme (or an eligible track) at TU/e for the 2027-2028 academic year, starting 1 September 2027
Meet the specific admission requirements of the Master's programme applied to
Completed a non-Dutch high school diploma or university bachelor's degree, or both
Have not completed higher education (university or university of applied sciences) in the Netherlands; exchange programmes are allowed
Have excellent academic results, demonstrated by a latest grade transcript GPA of at least 7.5/10
Will meet all requirements for obtaining a Dutch entry visa and residence permit
Not applying for a joint Master's with Tilburg University (JADS) or a European Double Degree programme
Have not been admitted on the basis of an admission decision from a previous intake
coverage: €7,500 per academic year for two years towards study costs
benefits: €7,500 per academic year for two years
Paid in monthly instalments to a Dutch (or SEPA) bank account
Approximately 35 awards: 20 for EEA students and 15 for non-EEA students
requirements: Confirm in the Master's application that you wish to be considered for the scholarship
Include a brief motivation explaining why you believe you are a strong candidate
Gain at least 45 ECTS in the first year to receive the second-year scholarship
required_documents: Brief motivation statement within the application
application_method: Apply for the Master's programme through the regular TU/e admissions route
Tick the scholarship option and include the motivation in that application
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Very competitive: the University states only about 2% of applicants receive the award. The TU/e International Office checks eligibility, then a Selection Committee consisting of the Rector Magnificus, Dean of Education, Director Finance & Control and Director Education & Student Affairs ranks applications. Selections are confirmed by the end of March 2027.
new_scholarship.notes: The scholarships are funded by the national Beethoven Programme, a Dutch government investment in the microchip sector. For non-EEA students part of the first-year award is funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science through the NL Scholarship; TU/e states you cannot apply for the NL Scholarship separately.

new_scholarship.name: World Changers Glasgow Scholarship
new_scholarship.description: The University of Glasgow awards a £5,000 tuition fee discount to new international postgraduate students from a published list of 19 countries who take up an eligible taught postgraduate place for September 2027 or January 2028 entry. The number of awards is stated as unlimited and the discount is applied automatically at registration, so no separate scholarship application is required. It cannot be combined with another University of Glasgow scholarship and is withdrawn automatically if the student is fully funded by an external sponsor.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be enrolled on an eligible University of Glasgow postgraduate programme for the September 2027 or January 2028 intake, hold nationality of one of 19 listed countries, and have international fee status.
eligibility: Enrolled on an eligible postgraduate programme for the September 2027 or January 2028 intake

National of one of the eligible countries: Brazil, Chile, Colombia, India, Indonesia, Israel, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Malaysia, Mexico, Nigeria, Pakistan, Palestine, Singapore, Syria, Thailand, Vietnam or Yemen
International fee status
requirements: Meet the entry criteria for one of the listed eligible postgraduate programmes
Hold international fee status and an eligible nationality
application_method: No separate application; the tuition fee discount is applied at registration and confirmed by email after the programme offer
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Awarded automatically to all applicants who meet the entry criteria; the University publishes no separate selection process or academic threshold.
new_scholarship.funding_period: one-off tuition fee discount applied at registration
new_scholarship.notes: This is the postgraduate World Changers award; the University also runs a separate undergraduate World Changers Global Excellence Scholarship, which is a distinct scheme.
